questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply right and then left.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Watches what other drivers are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems. This helps you stay safe even when other drivers are not paying attention.

questions.question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane show where pedestrians cross. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
You must give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is coming toward you. You must:

options.text: Drive to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, drive to the side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead has one-way traffic only.
Only one car can cross the bridge at a time.
The bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck coming the other way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck coming the other way.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the bridge ahead may be too narrow to safely meet or pass a truck. Be careful and be ready to slow down.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Every sudden stop wastes fuel when you have to speed up again. Looking ahead and slowing down gradually helps you use less gas.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at all intersections, whether the crosswalk is marked or not.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the bridge overhead has limited space. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, within 20 feet of an intersection, or within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends. Move to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends. Move to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending. Cars in the right lane must move to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that a side road is coming up. Watch for traffic entering from the side.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes to the right ahead.
Hiking trails to the right ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns. Do not make a U-turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with proper tread.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning: keep tires with good tread depth, keep tires at the right pressure, and slow down in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in that direction to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: Both the alcohol and drug effects become stronger.
Both the alcohol and drug effects become weaker.
Only the alcohol effect becomes weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the alcohol and drug effects become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine might affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you prevent drowsiness?

options.text: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take regular breaks to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are especially slippery right when rain starts.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your tires ride on a thin layer of water, oil, and dirt. Slow down when roads are wet or have standing water to keep traction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is on top and green is on bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: You do not need to leave as much space when following a motorcycle as when following a car. Is this true?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions. You should stay three to four seconds behind a motorcycle. This gives the rider time to avoid an emergency.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When road or weather conditions are not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when the road is wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when any condition makes driving unsafe. You can get a ticket for speeding even if you are at the posted speed limit if conditions are bad.

questions.question: Must a driver turning left at an intersection yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction?
questions.explanation: When you turn left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. Turn only when it is safe and no traffic is coming.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the vehicle to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: When driving to a place you do not know, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to guide you.
Plan your trip before you leave.
Know only roughly where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you leave.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance before you drive. Do not start with just a vague idea of where you are going. Check a map to find your destination before you start driving.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can make driving unsafe. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: How can you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and rear. Never drive alongside them and do not tailgate them.

questions.question: When can you legally pass another vehicle on the right?

options.text: When a vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you drive off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is a passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You may also pass on the right on a multilane road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clean.
Leave more space between you and the cars you are following.
Be careful around all other vehicles.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your following distance because slippery roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. Signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagging person, or a train whistle. Never drive around a lowered gate.
